why: I checked both must_not items against all 10 expect lines. Item 1: every line can be checked at the pull request's head. Most use local `run` proofs. One reads README.md. The CI line asks for the `test` check "on the pull request", which runs before merge. Publishing to npm is listed as a non-goal, not an expect line. Item 2: a tool with no tests would fail the expect line saying "`packages/jsonl-lint` has node:test tests covering the all-valid, invalid-rows, blank-line and missing-file cases. `npm ci && npm test` at the repo root runs them and exits 0." Its proof asks the verifier to see jsonl-lint tests in the npm test output and to read the test files. The package.json line also requires a `test` script that runs `node --test`. So a tool without tests run by npm test can't meet these lines. Neither forbidden thing appears.
